title: Frobenius twists: geometric integrality, scalar extension, and affine relative Frobenius
statement:
Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p>0$, with $p$ prime [def-weil-field], [def-pc-field-characteristic], and let $s:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ be a geometrically integral $k$-scheme [def-weil-scheme-over-base], [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. For $n\geq0$, put $\varphi_n(c)=c^{p^n}$ and
$$X_n=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k,\operatorname{Spec}(\varphi_n)}\operatorname{Spec}k,$$
with $k$-structure the second projection [def-pc-base-change]. Let $F_{X/k,n}:X\to X_n$ be the pair morphism with first projection $F_X^n$ and second projection $s$, where $F_X$ is absolute Frobenius [def-weil-absolute-frobenius-scheme], [def-weil-ring-frobenius]. Then $X_n$ is geometrically integral over $k$. More precisely, for every field extension $\iota:k\hookrightarrow k'$, the projection-compatible canonical identification is
$$(X_n)_{k'}\cong X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k,\operatorname{Spec}(\iota\circ\varphi_n)}\operatorname{Spec}k'.$$
For every affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq X$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], its twist $U_n\subseteq X_n$ is canonically $\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_{k,\varphi_n}k)$, these opens cover $X_n$, and $F_{X/k,n}^{-1}(U_n)=U$. The restriction $U\to U_n$ is induced by the $k$-algebra homomorphism
$$A\otimes_{k,\varphi_n}k\longrightarrow A,\qquad a\otimes b\longmapsto a^{p^n}s^\sharp(b),$$
where the source has $k$-structure through the second tensor factor. For $n=0$, the canonical identity-base-change isomorphism $X_0\cong X$ identifies $F_{X/k,0}$ with the identity and its affine ring map with $a\otimes b\mapsto a s^\sharp(b)$.

Geometric integrality follows by iterating the base change in its definition; the affine calculation and n=0 identity convention are the expanded calculation of parent step 6.

proof.text: Put $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $q=p^n$, $t=\operatorname{Spec}(\varphi_n)$, and write $\pi:X_n\to X$, $\rho:X_n\to S$ for the projections. By [def-weil-ring-frobenius], $\varphi_n$ is a unital ring homomorphism; it is injective because $c^q=0$ in a field implies $c=0$. Since $s^\sharp:k\to\mathcal O_X(V)$ is a unital ring homomorphism for every open $V\subseteq X$, $p\cdot1_{\mathcal O_X(V)}=s^\sharp(p\cdot1_k)=0$, so $X$ is of characteristic $p$ [def-weil-scheme-characteristic-p]; hence $F_X$ is defined and each $\mathcal O_X(V)$ carries the ring Frobenius of [def-weil-ring-frobenius]. Frobenius commutes with the structure map: on sheaves this is the identity $s^\sharp(c^q)=s^\sharp(c)^q$, and the underlying maps agree because absolute Frobenius is the identity on points [def-weil-absolute-frobenius-scheme]. Thus $sF_X^n=ts$. The universal property [def-pc-fibre-product] gives the unique pair map $F=(F_X^n,s):X\to X_n$ with $\pi F=F_X^n$ and $\rho F=s$. This also verifies that $F$ is a morphism over the second copy of $S$.

source.place: Tags 0CC9 (definition-relative-frobenius) and 0CCG (remark-n-fold-relative-frobenius), pair maps; Tag 0CC7 (lemma-frobenius-endomorphism-identity), proof.

proof.text: Let $\iota:k\hookrightarrow k'$ be arbitrary and set $h=\operatorname{Spec}(\iota):S'\to S$. A morphism $T\to (X_n)_{k'}$ is, by [def-pc-fibre-product], a triple $(a:T\to X,b:T\to S,c:T\to S')$ with $sa=tb$ and $b=hc$. Eliminating $b$ gives exactly the pair $(a,c)$ with $sa=thc$; conversely such a pair gives $(a,hc,c)$. Apply these constructions to the projections of the two products themselves. They give morphisms in both directions; each composite has the original projections, hence is the identity by uniqueness. This gives the canonical projection-compatible isomorphism $(X_n)_{k'}\cong X\times_{S,th}S'$. Contravariance of spectra [def-weil-affine-spectrum] gives $th=\operatorname{Spec}(\iota\circ\varphi_n)$. The composite $\iota\circ\varphi_n$ is a field embedding by step 1. Geometric integrality [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible] therefore makes this last fibre product integral. Since this holds for every $\iota$, $X_n$ with structure $\rho$ is geometrically integral. This argument uses no surjectivity of Frobenius and works over imperfect fields.

source.place: Tag 0CCG (remark-n-fold-relative-frobenius), first product; definition-geometrically-integral, clause (3), expanded using the fibre-product universal property.

proof.text: For an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq X$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product] with opens $U\subseteq X$ and $S\subseteq S$, over all of $S$. It identifies $U_n=U\times_{S,t}S$ with the open $\pi^{-1}(U)$ in $X_n$, compatibly with both projections. These opens cover, since the affine opens cover $X$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] to the maps $k\to A$, $c\mapsto s^\sharp(c)$, and $k\to k$, $c\mapsto c^q$. It identifies $U_n$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_{k,\varphi_n}k)$, with projection ring maps $a\mapsto a\otimes1$ and $b\mapsto1\otimes b$. Finally $F^{-1}(U_n)=(\pi F)^{-1}(U)=(F_X^n)^{-1}(U)=U$, because [def-weil-absolute-frobenius-scheme] says Frobenius is the identity on the underlying space.

Write $\alpha:k\to A$ for $s^\sharp$. The restriction of $F_X^n$ to $U$ is induced by the ring endomorphism $f(a)=a^q$ [def-weil-absolute-frobenius-scheme], [def-weil-ring-frobenius]. Set $g:k\to A$ to be $\alpha$. Use [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property] with base ring $R=k$, left algebra structure $\alpha$, right algebra structure $\varphi_n$, and target $A$ with $R$-structure $\alpha\varphi_n$. Then $f$ is $R$-linear since $f(\alpha(c)a)=\alpha(c^q)f(a)$, and $g$ is $R$-linear since $g(c^q b)=\alpha(c^q)g(b)$. The cited universal property supplies a ring map $H:A\otimes_{k,\varphi_n}k\to A$, $H(a\otimes b)=a^q\alpha(b)$. Explicitly the balancing relation $\alpha(c)a\otimes b=a\otimes c^q b$ has equal images $\alpha(c)^q a^q\alpha(b)=a^q\alpha(c^q b)$. Its composites with the two tensor-factor inclusions are $f$ and $g$. By the projection description of [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] and uniqueness in [def-pc-fibre-product], $\operatorname{Spec}H$ is exactly $F|_U$. For the source $k$-structure through the second factor, $H(1\otimes b)=\alpha(b)$, so $H$ is the asserted $k$-algebra homomorphism.

proof.text: If $n=0$, then $q=1$, $t=\mathrm{id}_S$ and $F_X^0=\mathrm{id}_X$. The first projection $\pi:X_0\to X$ has inverse the pair map $(\mathrm{id}_X,s)$: both composites are identities by their two projections and uniqueness in [def-pc-fibre-product]. The defining projections of $F$ in step 1 therefore identify $F_{X/k,0}$ with $\mathrm{id}_X$ under $\pi$. On each affine open step 4 reads $a\otimes b\mapsto a\alpha(b)$, with inverse $a\mapsto a\otimes1$: the tensor relation for the identity scalar map gives $a\alpha(b)\otimes1=a\otimes b$. This is the canonical identity-base-change isomorphism, and verifies the claimed affine convention.
